resources.string:
This module is created mostly for experienced users. Use it with extreme caution.
Wrong code provided here can potentially make your site unusable. You should always check the sections in which you're creating a custom menu item.
We provide this software “as is”, without warranty of any kind in case of a badly designed/wrong code is used.
We also recommend to always take with caution codes/solutions provided by 3rd parties for this module.
Cutom Menu Item Title to be processed
Warning. This must contain a valid and working PHP code. Use with extreme caution.

• The items above are custom menu handlers. Now you can use any items of the above as a system title string in a Snippet Meta Info type of menu sets.
  • Go to [Studio -> Navigation], choose the desired module, find in the list the set called "Snippet Meta Info", click it and from there you will be able to add custom items.
  • While adding a custom item give it the same name and title which you have in the Advanced Menu module's backend (for example "aqb_nl" for a new line). You can leave default the rest of the settings for a custom item.
  • When a name or title matches any of the value given at the "Menu Custom Item's Name and Title" it calls the relevant handler and replaces that item with the data, returned by the hanlder.
  • In case a handler is deactivated (greyed out in the table above) - a linked custom menu item is being replaced by an empty string.
  • Feel free to contact us in case you need help in creating, modifying or verifying some code/handler for a custom menu item. Or in case you have created a good usecase which can be useful for others and you'd like to contribute it to the public, so we could include it in the public version.

Available variables:
$aMenuItem - an array of a custom menu item's properties
$sMenuName - a string - name of a current menu set
$sModule - a string - name of a module to which the menu and the custom menu item belongs to
$iContentId - an integer value - ID of a content entry for which the menu is being rendered
$oMenuObject - an object - menu object used to render the menu
$aContentData - an array of a content entry's properties for which the menu is being rendered


Examples of using the common system items for showing a menu item:
return $oMenuObject->getUnitMetaItemText('Text'); - will display a simple text with a bullet icon on the left
return $oMenuObject->getUnitMetaItemLink('Text', ['href' => BX_DOL_URL_ROOT.'page/something']); - will display a link
return $oMenuObject->getUnitMetaItemButton('Text', ['onclick' => 'alert(\'Button clicked\')']); - will display a button
return $oMenuObject->getUnitMetaItemButtonSmall('Text', ['onclick' => 'alert(\'Button clicked\')']); - will display a small button
return $this->getUnitMetaItemNamedValue('TextName', 'Text'); - will display a named text value without a bullet icon on the left
return $this->getUnitMetaItemNamedValue('TextName', 'Text', 'Link'); - will display a named link without a bullet icon on the left
return 'Text'; - will display a raw text without a bullet on the left or any extra formatting
